aggressive_definition: Advanced incident prostate cancer, defined as regionally invasive or distant metastatic disease.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: risk for advanced prostate cancer (regionally invasive or distant metastatic, n = 123) decreased significantly with greater intake of supplemental vitamin E
study_design: Prospective cohort study with incident prostate cancers ascertained through linkage to the western Washington SEER registry.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: In a prospective design, 35,242 men recruited between 2000 and 2002 from western Washington State completed a questionnaire, including detailed questions about vitamin E and selenium supplement intake during the past 10 years from brand-specific multivitamins and single supplements.
reason: The prospective cohort analyzed both overall incident prostate cancer and incident advanced prostate cancer; the advanced endpoint was explicitly defined as regionally invasive or distant metastatic disease.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: There was no association between selenium supplementation and prostate cancer risk (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.62-1.3 for 10-year average intake >50 microg/day vs. non-use, p for trend 0.97).
estimate_classifications.reason: This selenium estimate concerns prostate cancer risk without restriction to advanced or another aggressive endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: A 10-year average intake of supplemental vitamin E was not associated with a reduced prostate cancer risk overall [hazard ratio (HR) 0.86, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.65-1.1 for > or =400 IU/day vs. non-use, p for trend 0.36]
estimate_classifications.reason: The abstract explicitly labels this vitamin E estimate as prostate cancer risk overall, so it must not be relabeled as aggressive.

additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: risk for advanced prostate cancer (regionally invasive or distant metastatic, n = 123) decreased significantly with greater intake of supplemental vitamin E (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.19-1.0 for 10-year average intake > or =400 IU/day vs. non-use, p for trend 0.03).
